title: [Dev] Game of Mods, a native Apple Silicon game where NPC conversation is powered by local AI, is out now in Steam Early Access
author: ArkavoOrg
selftext:
Game of Mods ships a 4-bit GGUF Gemma 4 E2B inside the .app and runs it on Metal, sized to fit an 8 GB M1 alongside rendering. Each NPC owns its own conversation cache so replies stay in character across turns. The model also emits an emotion label with each reply, which drives the VRM facial expression and modulates the synthesized voice. Apple's on-device speech recognition and synthesis handle the ears and mouth, so there is no cloud anywhere in the loop.

  
I'm the developer. Game of Mods is built for the Mac from the ground up: Metal 4 rendering, Apple speech recognition and synthesis, and a Gemma 4 dialogue model that ships inside the app and runs on your machine. No cloud, no account, no API key.



Walk up to a character and speak, or type. They answer aloud in their own voice, remember the conversation, and stay in character. The whole game plays by voice, including the menus, and every voice path has a keyboard twin.



There's a creator side too. Studio lets you build NPCs, player avatars, journeys and spaces as pure data (JSON + VRM), and publish them to Steam Workshop from inside the game.



Plays in English, German, Spanish, Japanese and Simplified Chinese.



Requirements: macOS 26, Apple Silicon. Playable on an 8 GB M1, 16 GB recommended. Intel Macs are not supported.



Early Access is honest about where it is: voice, conversation and characters are the strong part, environments are still simple.



$3 launch price through Sep 22 ($5 after). [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4029870/Game\_of\_Mods/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4029870/Game_of_Mods/)
